svg.title: Building an action dependency graph
svg.desc: Three AGVs on a six-cell map with timed plans; how to read one ADG vertex; the ADG with a Type 1 chain per AGV and two Type 2 edges from the location rule; a rotation that gives a cycle.
svg.metadata: ["Start from the timed plans: one row per action. The ADG gets one vertex per action, placed in a lane per robot. No edges yet.", "Type 1 edges: each robot's actions stay in order. AGV 1 does A -> B before B -> C; AGV 2 does D -> B before B -> E. AGV 3 has one action, so no Type 1 edge.", "Type 2, cell C: AGV 3 leaves C at t = 0 and AGV 1 enters C at t = 1. The earlier action must finish first, so the edge points from AGV 3's action to AGV 1's.", "Type 2, cell B: AGV 1 leaves B at t = 1 and AGV 2 enters B at t = 2, so AGV 1's B -> C must finish before AGV 2's D -> B starts. That is every edge: the ADG is done, and it keeps only these orders.", "The times only decided each edge's direction. When two robots swap or rotate at the same instant, the rule gives a cycle (inset): such a plan is safe only with perfectly synchronous moves."]

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Each action of each robot becomes a vertex. Type 1 edges keep each robot's own order; Type 2 edges say who must clear a cell before someone else enters it. The ADG keeps the plan's order and forgets its exact times.
